speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: asked	the Minister for Health what is the Ministry's progress on initiatives pertaining to public-private partnerships and whether there are plans for a wider rollout.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We have forged closer collaboration between the public and private sectors in recent years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Under CHAS, our Regional Health Systems are working with the private sector to set up Family Medicine Clinics, which focus on chronic disease management.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Our GP partners have also stepped up their effort in times of need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: More than 600 clinics supported the rollout of the Haze Subsidy Scheme when Singapore was faced with severe haze in 2013 and 2015.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For hospital care, MOH has worked with the private sector to provide subsidised care to our patients.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Patients can be sent to Raffles Hospital for emergency care, followed by inpatient or specialist outpatient care if required.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Another example is the collaboration with Parkway Hospitals to receive dengue patients from Changi General Hospital and Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH).

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For intermediate residential care, our acute hospitals have been in close collaboration with our Community Hospitals run by voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) on several fronts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: One example is the collaboration between TTSH and Ren Ci Community Hospital (RCCH) to jointly develop clinical governance standards, care pathways, manpower capacity and capability to facilitate the transfer of patients between the institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We work with private and VWO operators to operate aged care facilities, such as nursing homes and eldercare centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We are also partnering VWO operators to enhance palliative care services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: And as part of this development, we are working with Assisi Hospice to expand its capacity for its inpatient, home and day hospice services so that more end-of-life patients can benefit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: As part of our healthcare transformation plans, MOH will continue to explore opportunities to work together with the private sector to provide quality subsidised care for Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can I just find out pertaining to the Raffles Hospital and public hospital collaborations so far, what has been the feedback from patients as well as their caregivers, and whether there is a discussion or review to extend the programme beyond office hours as well as to other emergency departments also?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The collaboration with Raffles Hospital started since 2015.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And during the first few months of the collaboration, there were some teething issues, including how to work with the SCDF paramedics so that they know how and where to send the patients to.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is feedback that we collected through surveys.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The arrangements with Raffles Hospital can also give us some good learning points that we can extend to other partnerships between public and private hospitals.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And I think we can look at some of the suggestions that the Member has brought up, with the intent of seeing how we can work in collaboration with the private sector to provide good quality subsidised care for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
